title: Recurring problem reported to have begun
text: The resident reports that vehicle overrun, recurring mud and concern about the layout began after the household moved into the development. The history was later stated in correspondence held by NCC.
source: Resident account, later recorded in NCC’s 2023 disclosure.

title: Taylor Wimpey complaint 0014358 opened
text: A formal Taylor Wimpey complaint was recorded concerning vehicles parking on grass verges and causing tyre marks in the grass.
source: Taylor Wimpey complaint chain disclosed by NCC under FOI 11032506.

title: Taylor Wimpey described the land as a service strip
text: Taylor Wimpey stated that the strip was in its ownership, had to remain accessible and grassed, and was maintained through the development’s management arrangements. It said it could not enforce against individual drivers and closed the complaint.
source: Taylor Wimpey complaint response disclosed by NCC.

title: Further request about damage and responsibility
text: The resident again asked who was responsible for repairing the strip and linked the damage to the continuing absence of effective parking controls.

title: NCC circulated the issue across multiple services
text: The Complaints mailbox referred the matter to Planning Enforcement and Highways Programme. Planning Enforcement said it was not a planning matter. Parking Services confirmed there were no restrictions and said it could not assist. An approved highway layout plan was supplied.

title: Further NCC enquiry opened
text: A new enquiry sought action on parking, verge overrun, the service margin and the future adoption position.
source: NCC enquiry 7519613, disclosed in the complaints bundle.

title: NCC set out its pre-complaint position
text: NCC said the roads were not maintainable at public expense and no Section 38 agreement was in place. It said Highways Development Management and Legal were liaising with developers, Persimmon was understood to be lead developer, double yellow lines would not be pursued, and verge driving was attributed to road users. It also cited possible utilities as a reason not to expect fencing or planting within the service margin.

title: Resident requested inspection and protective measures
text: The resident asked NCC to inspect the site, ensure the current use did not depart from the approved layout and withhold adoption until suitable protective measures were installed.

title: Heavy vehicle movement recorded
text: Doorbell footage recorded a large truck passing across or immediately over the entrance-side area. The footage is relevant to the practical operation of the frontage, although the precise wheel path is partly obscured in some frames.

title: Formal Stage 1 complaint and EIR request submitted
text: The resident formally complained about the layout, vehicle overrun, pedestrian risk and the absence of preventative measures. A separate request sought Road Safety Audit and Section 38 records.

title: NCC accepted the Stage 1 complaint
text: NCC said it would review earlier responses alongside the current concerns and handle the Road Safety Audit records separately under the Environmental Information Regulations.

title: Detailed evidence and clarification supplied
text: The resident clarified that the primary complaint concerned layout and recurring encroachment rather than routine grass maintenance. Photographs, vehicle evidence, the reported fleet incident and technical arguments were submitted.

title: Stage 1 complaint not upheld
text: NCC said the shared-surface layout complied with guidance and that no evidence showed a safety risk requiring intervention. It separated vehicle use of the verge from the safety of the layout and rejected fencing or planting on service-margin grounds.

title: EIR confirmed no RSA and no Section 38 agreement
text: NCC stated that no Road Safety Audit existed and no Section 38 agreement was in place. It supplied drawings described as technically approved; several were marked preliminary. A follow-up confirmed that no recorded RSAs were held for this part of the development.
source: NCC EIR response 9318765 and follow-up confirmation.

title: Stage 2 review requested
text: The resident challenged the evidential basis of Stage 1, reliance on recorded injury incidents, treatment of the reported 2022 council-vehicle incident, use of Manual for Streets and the generic utilities objection.

title: NCC issued its final Stage 2 response
text: NCC did not uphold the complaint. It accepted that the photographs showed verge overrun and acknowledged that the team had not fully taken into account the fleet manoeuvring information. It nevertheless relied on injury-collision data and maintained that practical and technical concerns justified refusing a knee rail.

title: Taylor Wimpey reinstated the strip
text: The damaged grassed area was repaired and reseeded.
source: Resident records and Taylor Wimpey correspondence.

title: More than five further crossings documented
text: Within approximately 50 hours of reinstatement, the resident documented more than five further vehicle crossings of the newly repaired strip.

title: Council-wide information request submitted
text: The resident requested records from 2018 onwards covering complaints, internal and external communications, adoption, maintenance, inspections and proposed traffic-management measures.

title: Case 001 summary published
text: VergeOverrunUK published the first public summary of the case, with supporting images and documents retained pending redaction.

title: Taylor Wimpey reported an NCC pause
text: Taylor Wimpey informed the resident that NCC had requested all further consideration and works to be paused because the resident was said to be pursuing a claim or separate legal avenue.
source: Taylor Wimpey correspondence; the underlying NCC instruction has not yet been disclosed.

title: Taylor Wimpey closed its complaint
text: Taylor Wimpey issued a final response and closed the matter. It attributed to NCC a position that proposals could not be considered and that adoption of the strip and wider development would not progress while the unspecified matter remained unresolved.

title: FOI response disclosed historic records but raised search questions
text: NCC stated that its “area office” held no relevant records, yet supplied a 95-page complaints bundle and Planning records documenting complaints, internal referrals and Taylor Wimpey material. An internal review is being prepared to clarify the council-wide searches and the correct information-access regime.
source: NCC FOI response 11032506 and four disclosure attachments.

title: NCC asked to confirm or correct Taylor Wimpey’s account
text: The resident asked NCC to identify the alleged claim or process, the decision-maker and date, the basis of the pause, the event that would end it, and whether Taylor Wimpey may resume preparing proposals while liability remains reserved.

title: Ombudsman and information-rights steps being prepared
text: The Council’s complaint procedure is complete. The resident is preparing an LGSCO complaint focused on the quality of the investigation and a separate internal review and supplementary EIR request concerning the disclosure searches and reported pause.
